one_liner: Apify has a broad REST API (v2, OpenAPI published) with self-serve API-token auth, OAuth 2.0 for integrations, and (per registry and catalog signals) an official MCP server.
auth_notes: Users generate an API token in Console and send it as a Bearer header (recommended) or token query param. The integration guide says Apify supports OAuth 2.0 and API token. The pages don't show how a third party gets OAuth client credentials, so API token stays primary.
access_notes: Any user can create an API token in Console. The fetched pages describe Apify as freemium but give no explicit free-plan or credit details, so the free-tier terms are unverified.
blocker_notes: Usage is billed against platform credits. The exact free allowance isn't confirmed by the fetched pages.

evidence.quote: You can create an API token on the [Integrations](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations) page in the Apify Console.
Add the token to your request's `Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>`.
*OAuth 2.0* - Use OAuth 2.0 to allow users to authorize your integration without sharing their credentials.
| **Freemium** | Basic access is free; advanced features or higher limits require payment. | Spotify APIs, GitHub APIs, Apify APIs |
The API is organized around [RESTful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer) HTTP endpoints.
You can download the complete OpenAPI schema of Apify API in the [YAML](http://docs.apify.com/api/openapi.yaml) or [JSON](http://docs.apify.com/api/openapi.json) formats.
